## Welcome to the OHDSI-UK training

## Aims of the analytics track

. . .

By the end of the training:

-   Be able to conduct descriptive analyses using R with data in the OMOP CDM format

-   Understand how to approach writing bespoke code for complex studies

-   Know where to look for help

## What to expect

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
<img src="images/programming.gif" alt="Programming gif" style="height: 600px;"/>
:::

## What to expect

. . .

-   Quarto presentations - most presentations correspond to an R package that works with data in the OMOP CDM format.

-   "Your Turn" exercises - during presentations where you can practice using the package (solutions will be on the next slide, but first try without looking at these!)

-   General practical - time to apply what you have learned during the training.

## Post-It notes

. . .

-   Green - all good, no code currently running

-   Yellow - code running

-   Red - help me!

## Set up

[**Download the needed data**](https://github.com/oxford-pharmacoepi/AnalyticsTrack2026/archive/refs/heads/main.zip)


- Contains the datasets you will need for today

- Open the *Analytics track* project with RStudio

- Copy the databases to the *Back up* folder

- Run the `Setup.R` script in the *Your turn* folder

## Schedule 

| Time | Session |
| --- | --------- |
| 10.30 - 13.00 | • Creating a CDM reference with [CDMConnector](https://darwin-eu.github.io/CDMConnector/) <br> • Characterise the OMOP CDM instance with [OmopSketch](https://ohdsi.github.io/OmopSketch/) <br> • Writing custom queries using [PatientProfiles](https://darwin-eu.github.io/PatientProfiles/) and [dbplyr](https://dbplyr.tidyverse.org) |
| 13.00 - 14.00 | *Lunch break (Room D)* |
| 14:00 - 16.30 | • Creating cohorts using [CohortConstructor](https://ohdsi.github.io/CohortConstructor/) <br> • Characterise cohorts using [CohortCharacteristics](https://darwin-eu.github.io/CohortCharacteristics/) <br> • Evaluating cohorts using [PhenotypeR](https://ohdsi.github.io/PhenotypeR/) |
